questions.question: Matched to their plate boundaries, the three tectonic forces are:
options: Compression at convergent, tension at divergent, shearing at transform boundaries
Tension at convergent, compression at divergent, shearing at all three
Shearing at convergent, tension at transform, compression at divergent boundaries
All three occur only at transform boundaries

questions.question: Deep in the crust, rock tends to FOLD rather than fault because it is:
options: Colder and more brittle at depth
Hot and confined by pressure on every side, so it deforms plastically without fracturing

questions.question: Which rock is MOST likely to fracture rather than fold?
The full sequence of rock deformation under growing stress is:
options: Elastic, plastic, fractured, displaced — the same order that will explain earthquakes

subtopics.title: Folds — Anticlines, Synclines and the Fold Family

questions.question: An anticline and a syncline are, respectively:
options: An upfold arching to a crest, and a downfold sagging to a trough
Two names for the same structure

questions.question: Once erosion bites into an anticline, the rocks exposed at its core are the:
options: Youngest, because they were deposited last
OLDEST, because folding lifted the deepest layers highest
Volcanic, because magma fills every fold

questions.question: In order of increasing compression, the fold family runs:
Inversion of relief occurs because:
options: Synclines are always pushed higher than anticlines
Folding turns the strata upside down
The stretched, cracked crest of an anticline erodes fastest, so the arch may become a valley while the tightly squeezed syncline survives as high ground

subtopics.title: Faults and the Landforms They Make

questions.question: A fracture in the crust only qualifies as a FAULT once:
options: The rock on either side has actually moved
It is longer than one kilometre

questions.question: In a NORMAL fault, produced by tension:
options: The hanging wall is driven up over the footwall
The hanging wall slips DOWN the fault plane relative to the footwall, often leaving a fault scarp

questions.question: A graben and a horst are, respectively:
options: Two names for a fold mountain
A tilted block and a step fault
A central block DROPPED between parallel faults (a rift valley at the surface) and a central block left STANDING (a block mountain)
A volcanic crater and its cone

questions.question: The Black Forest and the Vosges, flanking the Rhine rift valley, are examples of:
options: Twin HORSTS — block mountains standing on either side of a graben

subtopics.title: The Cape Fold Mountains — and Describing Structures in Words

questions.question: The Cape Fold Mountains were formed when:
options: Compression during the assembly of Gondwana, roughly 250 to 280 million years ago, buckled the hard quartzitic sandstones of the Cape Supergroup
A volcano erupted through the Western Cape
Tension opened a rift valley near Ceres
Glaciers carved the ranges during an ice age

questions.question: The two trends of the Cape Fold ranges are:
options: Both running exactly east to west
Roughly north-south ranges like the Olifants River Mountains and Piketberg, and roughly west-east ranges like the Riviersonderend and Tsitsikamma, knotting together around Ceres

questions.question: Passes such as Michell's Pass, the Tradouw Pass and Meiringspoort exist because:
options: The ranges are too low to matter
Each folded range is a genuine wall, so roads cross only where a gap was found or forced

questions.question: The fixed order for describing any structure in words is:
options: The force, the response, the shape, the landform

questions.question: Pressing a lump of dough inward from both sides until it humps into ridges demonstrates:
options: Compression building folds — the force where plates drive together

questions.question: The dough and the rusk stand for the two ways rock can respond to force, namely:
options: Bending like warm, deep, slowly stressed rock, or snapping like cold, shallow, suddenly stressed rock

questions.question: Which trio decides whether rock folds or faults?
options: Depth and temperature, the speed of the force, and the rock type

subtopics.title: Hills, Hollows and the Surprise Valley

questions.question: In the wavy cross-section, every hump and every dip are, in order:
options: An anticline and a syncline, sharing their sloping limbs

questions.question: The five-stage story of a fold under growing squeeze is:
options: Torn, lying down, overhanging, leaning, even
Even, leaning, overhanging, lying down, torn — symmetrical to overthrust
Leaning, even, torn, overhanging, lying down

questions.question: The rolled magazine whose spine creases on the outside of the bend explains why:
options: An anticline's crest is stretched and cracked, so erosion attacks it hardest — setting up inversion of relief

questions.question: After inversion of relief, the landscape shows:
options: Every anticline standing as a peak
Former arches hollowed into valleys while former troughs stand as ridges — upside down relative to the structure

questions.question: A paving slab settled LOWER than its neighbour along the crack models:
options: A normal fault from tension, printing a fault scarp on the landscape
A shear fault from sideways creep

questions.question: A painted line across two slabs that no longer joins, though neither slab is higher, models:
options: A SHEAR fault — offset with no step, the San Andreas signature at continental size

questions.question: With three slabs, letting the middle one sink between its neighbours gives the shape of:
options: A rift valley — a flat dropped floor between two straight walls, the East African Rift in miniature

questions.question: The one-glance test for folded against faulted country is:
options: Green country is folded; brown is faulted
High country is folded; low is faulted
Wet country is folded; dry is faulted
Curves mean the rock bent; ruler-straight scarps, flat-topped blocks and stepped edges mean it broke
